title: Pleasant Hill Lights Up Tonight With Diwali Night Market Celebration
excerpt: The Chilpancingo Park market marks the Festival of Lights on Friday, November 6, 2026, from 5 to 9 p.m., with an illuminated sculpture show, live performances, a DJ and family activities.
body:
Pleasant Hill will mark Diwali with light, music and food tonight, Friday, November 6, 2026, as the Pleasant Hill Night Market turns its regular evening in Chilpancingo Park into a Festival of Lights celebration from 5 p.m. to 9 p.m.

According to the Pleasant Hill Families weekly events listing, tonight's market features an illuminated sculpture show, live performances and a live DJ, alongside family activities including a petting zoo, a bounce house, a face painter and a balloon twister. Food and local vendors will also be on site, with purchases for a fee.

  • Pleasant Hill's Night Market holds a Diwali Festival of Lights celebration tonight, Friday, November 6, 2026, from 5 p.m. to 9 p.m. in Chilpancingo Park.
  • The evening features an illuminated sculpture show, live performances, a live DJ, a petting zoo, a bounce house, face painting and a balloon twister, per the Pleasant Hill Families listing.
  • SF FunCheap lists entry as free; food and local vendor purchases are for a fee, according to the events listing.
  • The City of Pleasant Hill says the Night Market series runs on the first and third Fridays of the month through November 20, 2026.

The market is a recurring city series, not a one-off festival. The City of Pleasant Hill's Night Market page says the series launched on Friday, May 1, 2026, and continues on the first and third Fridays of each month, 5:00 to 9:00 p.m. in Chilpancingo Park through November 20, 2026. Across the season, the city lists food vendors, a beer truck, local merchandise vendors and live music, plus activities such as corn hole, face painting and balloon animals, and wellness, kids and pet zones.

Tonight's Diwali theme layers a South Asian festival onto that format. Diwali, the Festival of Lights celebrated by Hindus, Jains, Sikhs and some Buddhists, marks the triumph of light over darkness, and public celebrations in the Bay Area have become a regular way for diaspora families to share the festival with neighbours who may be encountering it for the first time. An illuminated sculpture show fits that theme directly, bringing the festival's central image — light pushed back against the dark — into a public park after sunset.

For families, the practical draw is the mix in one place and in one short evening window. The listing for tonight combines performances and a DJ with activities aimed at children, including the petting zoo, bounce house, face painter and balloon twister, while food and local vendors give adults a reason to stay for dinner rather than treat the visit as a brief stop. Because the market ends at 9 p.m., it is an after-school and after-work outing rather than a late night.

Listings differ in how they describe where tonight sits in the season, so visitors should check the city's page before travelling if plans change. The event listing on SF FunCheap's Pleasant Hill Night Market page confirms tonight's date and hours — Friday, November 6, 2026, 5:00 p.m. to 9:00 p.m. — and gives the park address as 200 Golf Club Rd, Pleasant Hill, CA.

Plan your visit

  • Date: Friday, November 6, 2026 — tonight
  • Time: 5:00 p.m. to 9:00 p.m.
  • Venue: Chilpancingo Park, Pleasant Hill
  • Address: 200 Golf Club Rd, Pleasant Hill, CA (per SF FunCheap listing)
  • Admission: SF FunCheap lists cost as FREE; food and local vendors are for a fee, per the Pleasant Hill Families listing. Check the City of Pleasant Hill page for any last-minute changes.
  • Programme: Illuminated sculpture show, live performances, live DJ, petting zoo, bounce house, face painter and balloon twister, per the Pleasant Hill Families listing.

For the East Bay's Indian diaspora, the value is local. A Diwali celebration in a neighbourhood park in Pleasant Hill means families in Contra Costa County do not have to travel into San Francisco or the South Bay to mark the festival in public, and children can experience it alongside classmates and neighbours. For everyone else, tonight is a straightforward invitation: arrive before dark, stay for the lights, and leave with dinner from a local vendor.
